correctness.rationale: Uniform outer-product factorization has exactly q−1 gauges; any two entries are independent uniform products, yielding exact finite covariance. The row/column category multinomial vectors have independent CLTs and, after canceling all linear terms, produce the centered Gaussian bilinear convolution at scale sqrt(mn). Finite-group characters diagonalize the bilinear form, with singular values equal to nontrivial Fourier coefficients and the displayed determinant product; single-label marginals and fourth cumulants follow. The finite rational enumeration and independent numerical Fourier determinant test replay successfully; these finite checks do not substitute for the all-dimensional CLT argument.

originality.rationale: The specific contribution is the full-support-conditioned joint nonzero-value histogram law, including explicit character-product characteristic function and product-normal/Laplace marginals, not the older unconditional Gaussian fixed-rank result or its bilinear Fourier mechanism. Sanna (2023), Lemma 5.4, contains closely related bilinear Fourier decompositions, directly acknowledged, but its theorem and proof concern unconditional random matrix entries and do not state the uniform full-support conditional joint law. Chan–Xiong (2024) concerns unconditional growing-rank CLTs. Migler–Morrison–Ogle (2006) counts total nonzero weight, constant in the present conditional ensemble. Searches of published-finding corpus and accessible historical claims found no equivalent conditional theorem, subject to residual priority risks.
residual_risks: Sanna Lemma 5.4 contains a substantially similar factorized bilinear Fourier decomposition, from which a specialist could deduce the conditioned law; only the explicitly evaluated conditional result is assessed.
An equivalent conditioned multivariate law could appear in unindexed earlier coding-theory, rank-one random matrix, or finite-group probability literature.
Neither absence from semantic search nor partition by research category proves absolute originality.

value.rationale: The natural full-support locus of rank-one finite-field matrices is exponentially rare under unconditional sampling, so its nonzero-label histogram fluctuations are invisible to existing unconditional CLTs. The result shows pairwise independent matrix entries with genuinely non-Gaussian global count fluctuations, identifies the complete group-theoretic joint law, and exhibits sharp product-normal and Laplace small-field specializations. These give an interpretable algebraic boundary between unconditional Gaussian and conditioned second-chaos behavior.
